evidence.evidence_text: Large language models (LLMs) can now access a wide range of external tools, thanks to the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Large language models (LLMs) can now access a wide range of external tools, thanks to the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
This greatly expands their abilities as various agents.
However, LLMs rely entirely on the text descriptions of tools to decide which ones to use—a process that is surprisingly fragile.

In this work, we expose a vulnerability in prevalent tool/function-calling protocols by investigating a series of edits to tool descriptions, some of which can drastically increase a tool’s usage from LLMs when competing with alternatives.
Through controlled experiments, we show that tools with properly edited descriptions receive over 10 times more usage from GPT-4.1 and Qwen2.5-7B than tools with original descriptions.
